rights, c) gender equity and equality (as well as increased male participation in 
solidifying family life and the socialization of children), and facilitate increased 
access of children and lactating and pregnant women to adequate nutrition at the 
regional and community levels. 
The UNCT will support and promote the development of strong mechanisms for participatory approaches 
and greater accountability with a view to having women and vulnerable groups integrally involved in 
decision-making, planning, priority setting and monitoring at the local level and to promote equality of 
access to and control over resources. The UNCT will collaborate with all stakeholders to strengthen 
decentralized governance capacity, delivery of basic social services, and the provision of access to 
information on reproductive health, STDs/ HIV/ AIDS. 
Because adolescent sex has emerged as one of the key reasons for both poverty and the spread of 
HIV/AIDS, the UNCT will build on and expand the pilot Adolescent Sexual Reproductive Health (ASRH) 
project launched by UNFPA in partnership with Government and the Guyana Family Planning Association 
(GFPA). Emphasis will be placed not only on sex education but also on the promotion of healthy lifestyles. 
The promotion of reproductive rights will seek to involve men, emphasize their responsibilities, and 
advocate joint responsibility in family planning. Continued support will be given to the unmet need for 
contraceptives and protection against STDs/HIV/AIDS. Because increased drug use has emerged as a 
major contributor to the spread of HIV/AIDS, the UNCT will build on the Save Our Own Now (SOON) 
project that targets the adolescent population. 
The UNCT will work with Government to improve the nutritional status of children, lactating mothers, and 
pregnant women through increased energy and micronutrient in-take. Support for the fortification of 
commonly used foods and making iron supplements available to pregnant women will continue. 
C. Right to Health 
While Government accords a high priority to health promotion and prevention activities, Guyana is still far 
from attaining the goal of equity in the access to the highest attainable health by all as articulated under the 
ICESCR, CEDAW, and CRC. Access continues to elude the most vulnerable (women and children, the 
rural population, the poor, the under-privileged, the marginalized). The UNCT will continue to exploit the 
comparative advantage of its specialized agencies and programmes to target vulnerable groups, facilitate 
analyses and understanding of the inhibiting factors, and address the crosscutting issues that are critical for 
the development of the health system in general and health services for the vulnerable population in 
particular. 
To contribute to a closure of the gap between what prevails currently and achievement of the health-related 
goals set at various global conferences (ICPD, Beijing, WSC, WSSD), the objective of UNCT assistance 
and support to Government will be to support activities which promote opportunities to improve health 
status for all. The proposed strategies to achieve this will include the strategies as outlined in the 
Caribbean Charter of Health promotion. 
The UNCT assistance strategy will focus on: 
 Formulating health-related public policy 
 Creating supportive environments 14
 Developing personal health skills 
 Re-orienting health services 
 Building alliances 
 Empowering communities to achieve well-being. 
More specifically, the UNCT will: 
(i) Provide support to health system research and disaggregated baseline and 
programme data collection and analysis in order to improve health system outreach 
to the most under served communities including the indigenous population as well 
as to better inform policy and decision-making. 
Assistance will be directed at addressing the inter-related issues of (a) the role of public, private, and NGO 
participation and financing, and (b) the critical task of human resources development for and in the health 
sector. The acute shortage of trained health personnel--like the dearth of adequate, gender-disaggregated 
data—plays a major role in placing health services out of the reach of the most deprived. 
(ii) Provide support to inter- and intra-sectoral coordination in order to improve health 
system efficiency especially in respect of the primary health care system. 
Inter-sectoral coordination between the health sector and other sectors like education, water and sanitation, 
and the environment is indispensable for understanding and meaningfully addressing issues of child 
survival, reproductive health in rural areas, child neglect, preventable communicable diseases, how best to 
modify lifestyles, and the impact of the domestic environment. Inter-sectoral cooperation facilitates the 
targeting of interventions and maximizes the gains from a given bundle of resources. The UNCT is well 
placed to enhance this cooperation and collaboration and indeed, is already fostering it. 
UNCT will direct greater support in the areas of developing appropriate guidelines and mechanisms for 
functional cooperation among the public, private, and NGO sub-sectors and for the integrated management 
of school health, water, and sanitation programmes. Effective coordination between organizations involved 
in human resources planning, training, and utilization in the health sector will also be strengthened. The 
UNCT will continue to promote bilateral cooperation between Guyana and other countries. 
(iii) Contribute to strengthening decentralized health management capacity, effective 
participation of beneficiaries, and accountability of the system to both beneficiaries 
and the policymaking directorate. 
Improved health care delivery requires, among other things, strengthened management capacity at all 
levels and more efficient use of resources, particularly of human resources. In this regard, efforts aimed at 
promoting the full participation of communities in improving service delivery and management merits 
special attention. Individuals have to be mobilized and empowered to contribute to better health care in 
their communities as well as to demand better service and accountability from those who manage the 
system. 
The UNCT subscription to a decentralized system will translate into (a) advocacy of deployment policies 
that are informed by local needs, (b) support for the strengthening of district health systems for capacity 
building in health management, (c) the redefinition of central-level roles and responsibilities in a 15
decentralized health care delivery system, and (d) adequate female representation on management boards 
at all levels. 
(iv) Assist Government to increase access to gender-sensitive and quality services 
(including adolescent sexual and reproductive health services) and to assure 
effective mainstream HIV/AIDS prevention and management into existing 
programmes. 
UNCT will devote considerable effort to re-orient the health care delivery system to provide gendersensitive and quality services that are accessible to women who are currently disadvantaged. Advocacy, 
advice, and resources will be targeted to improve service delivery points and ensure that health facilities 
have sufficient essential drugs and equipment, trained (female) personnel, and basic amenities (e.g. 
adequate water and sanitation and refrigerated storage facilities). The UNCT will also seek to assist 
Government to improve the referral systems that link the different levels and types of health services and to 
develop structured linkages with private and NGO health providers. 
UNCT will advocate and assist in the gender sensitization of health personnel and will support programmes 
that pursue (a) the realization of safe motherhood targets, (b) a reduction in the incidence of domestic 
violence, and (c) the mainstreaming of reproductive health and improved family planning methods. Support 
will be directed at integrating STDs and HIV/AIDS impact awareness into all UN programmes through 
social mobilization and participation and at facilitating an expanded multi-sectoral response to the spread of 
HIV/AIDS. 
D. Right to education, culture and science 
With respect to education, culture, and science, Guyana needs to do much more in pursuit of the goals 
articulated in international conventions like the CEDAW, IESCR, and CRC that it has ratified. The UNCT 
activities, therefore, will be guided by a strategy that emphasizes assistance and advise to Government in 
its attempt to make access to all levels of education, access to cultural life, and access to the benefits of 
science and technology the right of every Guyanese. The UNCT strategy embraces the propagating of the 
awareness of these rights to all sections of the populace. 
More specifically, the UNCT will: 
(i) Provide assistance to improve the provision of quality learning, including 
infrastructure and provision of food and health services through increased 
partnerships and capacity-building. 
The UNCT considers education one of the principal weapons for combating poverty and rights denial, and 
believes that at all levels of education emphasis should be placed on quality. With regards basic education, 
support will be given to building the capacity of NGOs and private sector partners in education, with a view 
to ensuring that there exists quality post-literacy education and vocational skills and life-long learning 
opportunities. 
Support will address: 
(a) Raising the quality of learning environments through the: 16
 quality of accredited and in-service teacher training 
 use of supplementary materials in classrooms, and 
 use of continuous assessment. 
(b) Ensuring that nursery level educational facilities address also child survival, growth, and 
development and that these learning environments are child-friendly. 
(c) Developing and strengthening the capacity of NGOs and community groups to support 
children's learning and to monitor teacher performance. 
(d) Strengthening capacity to target and monitor the various literacy and non-formal basic 
education initiatives at the community level and to link these to subsequent continuous 
learning, functional skills, and income generating opportunities. 
(e) Strengthening resource centres and various levels of the MOE to facilitate their delivery of 
professional support to schools and teachers. 
(f) Strengthening management information systems through the systematic collection of 
disaggregated data. 
(ii) Promote a human rights culture and peace through education. 
The UNCT will support mass campaigns that involve the media, local leaders, schools, and civil society 
with a view to promoting peace, tolerance, and appreciation of Guyana’s diversity. Support will be given to 
initiatives that seek to integrate the teaching of tolerance and respect for ethnic and other differences into 
the formal school system. 
The UNCT will work with Government and civil society (NGOs, CBOs, the private sector, political leaders, 
religious leaders, etc.) to ensure that the rights to cultural life are fulfilled. In this respect, the UNCT will 
support the celebration of special festivals and cultural events, the revitalization of traditional events, the 
protection and rehabilitation of heritage sites, and other such initiatives that serve to help individual groups 
in society to recognize and accept each others' uniqueness and provide opportunities for mutual respect of 
differences. 
(iii) Support the innovative propagation of Information Technology (IT) and its access by 
the most deprived. 
The UNCT recognizes that the poorest sections of the populace are excluded from the benefits of IT for 
reasons of access (electricity, telephone line, Internet-ready computer, etc.) and illiteracy among others. 
The UNCT is also aware that in societies that are relatively traditional, like Guyana, the wider and easier 
access to information that IT permits have the potential to upset traditional patterns of information 
dissemination and sharing that could limit IT potential as an agent of change. 
However, the UNCT will continue to support the innovative use of appropriate technologies, especially 
those that are labour-saving, those that relieve the drudgery of women, and those that aid poor households 
to generate income. Indeed, where possible, the UNCT will strengthen the links between such 
technologies and the generation of income through community learning facilities and non-formal education. 17
At the same time, the UNCT recognizes the increasing influence of information technology and its potential 
to exert positive influences on the life chances of the poor and assist Guyana to leapfrog along the 
development continuum. In this regard, the UNCT will continue to support Government in partnership with 
the private sector to promote greater and more equitable access to information technology, especially in the 
area of communications. The Sustainable Development Networking Programme (SDNP) initiative, 
designed to assist Government entities and the members of relatively poor communities to benefit from 
internet access, will be intensified. 
E. The right to work 
A people that enjoy adequate standards of living and access to adequate health services and education are 
likely to enjoy also greater access to work. Conversely, if the right to work is respected, protected, and 
fulfilled, people are likely to have access to a better standard of living. The UNCT will focus especially on 
two of the core issues of the right to work as articulated in international conventions like the IECSR, ILO, 
CEDAW, WSSD, and CRC, namely, the right to earn a living and the right to just, safe, and healthy work 
conditions. 
The UNCT will extend support to the creation of an environment conducive to appropriate policy 
formulation, policy implementation, and the building of capacity to undertake these activities. The objective 
of the UNCT assistance will be to increase opportunities for the most deprived persons to earn a decent 
living, in pursuit of the goal of universal access to paid employment articulated in the WSSD. The UNCT 
strategy will support appropriate macro-economic policies and promote outreach to the deprived. The 
UNCT will collaborate with the MFIs and support, by way of advocacy, their work to improve Guyana’s 
macro-economic policy environment with a view to stimulating broad-based and sustainable growth. 
More specifically, the UNCT will: 
(i) Support the development of a comprehensive employment policy and the removal of 
obstacles to the right to earn a living. 
The UNCT will support Government’s employment promotion initiatives especially where the selection of 
technology, geographic location, and strategies are designed to promote employment opportunities for the 
most vulnerable groups. Further, policy formulation support will be given to Government to develop 
initiatives that combine entrepreneurship instruction with training and assistance in the areas of marketing, 
management, and finance to generate self-employment or to respond to obvious labour market needs. 
Assistance will also be directed at the Ministry of Health and Labour to assist in the development and 
implementation of appropriate occupational health and safety policies and to create the framework for 
effective enforcement. 
(ii) Assist in strengthening the economic regulatory framework and policy in order to 
address the challenges of globalization while ensuring pro-poor growth 
Much work remains to be done on improving the regulatory framework and policy design instruments to 
enable private sector industries to innovate, introduce modern technologies and processes, compete 
internationally, and “hold their own” in regional and global markets. Initiatives to reorient frameworks, 
instruments, and incentives for export promotion need to continue. The cultivation of an investment friendly 
environment is far from complete. Domestic firms continue to need assistance in the acquisition and 18
effective management of modern technologies and techniques. Appropriate databases and management 
information systems need to be developed. The UNCT is well placed to make a meaningful contribution to 
work in these and other areas, such as: 
 Facilitating collaborative and participatory approaches in policy design, implementation, monitoring, 
and evaluation of strategies and programmes to promote manufacturing. 
 Assisting stakeholders to build the capabilities to pursue environmentally sustainable industrial 
development. 
 Assisting the competent institutions to augment their services and better coordinate and assist the 
development efforts of small and medium enterprises (SMEs) by way of assistance in the areas of 
credit, training, technology, marketing, and information. 
 Assessing the impact of structural adjustment on the poor with a view to aiding in the design and 
implementation of ameliorating negative impacts and promoting best practices. 
The UNCT intends to offer this type of assistance in the interest of promoting equitable and broad-based 
growth and assisting Guyana to better deal with globalization. 
(iii) Promote access to employment opportunities in rural areas. 
The UNCT believes that given Guyana's abundance and variety of natural resources, emphasis on 
sustainable livelihoods, Eco-tourism, and community forestry projects holds tremendous potential for
employment generation among the persons residing in the hinterland of the country, especially the poor 
and deprived Amerindians. As such, the UN System agencies will continue to concentrate on innovative 
projects in these areas. For example, the community-based Tree and Forest Product Enterprise is an area 
in which FAO can provide technical assistance. Currently, the Forest Officer based at FAO's Sub-regional 
Office in Barbados collaborates with the Guyana Forestry Commission (GFC) and FAO Headquarters is 
exploring mechanisms to strengthen the GFCs capacity to undertake participatory processes. 
Further, the UNCT intends to continue to assist Government to promote better standards of education, 
skills, and entrepreneurial capabilities to improve the flexibility of rural communities and the labour mobility 
of their members, especially women. Support for projects which build on the success of Iwokrama will 
continue to loom large in the UNCT portfolio, as will initiatives in the areas of business incubation and 
entrepreneurial training, and the mobilization of youths and women farmers to more effectively access 
credit, extension services, technology and training programmes. Advocacy will continue to be directed at 
line agencies with a view to reducing traditional gender biases in programmes and operations and to 
encourage the promotion of farm enterprises and activities that lend themselves to women’s empowerment. 
F. Civil and political rights 
The UN System believes that the realization of civil and political rights are integral to progress in the 
spheres of economic, social and cultural rights and that good governance is an imperative for ensuring a 
non-discrimination, participation, and accountability in the development process. In keeping with the thrust 
of the various international conferences and conventions, the UNCT assistance will place particular 
attention on liberty and the security of person, democracy and participation, and the administration of 
justice. The UNCT recognizes that the poorest segments of the population often suffer the greatest abuse 19
in relation to these rights and that poverty reduction enhances their chances of redeeming these rights. 
The UNCT assistance directed at civil and political rights will seek to contribute to the goals set by the 
WCHR by pursuing the following objectives: 
 To support amendment and reform of all laws and administrative procedures that are inconsistent 
with the civil and political rights guaranteed in the Constitution and the ICCPR. 
 To support the development of affirmative action policies and programmes for women and 
minorities. 
 To support non-governmental organizations and civil institutions such as Parliament, the Guyana 
Human Rights Commission (GHRC), and the Office of the Ombudsman and/or initiatives that foster 
democracy, accountability, and transparency. 
 To sensitize the judicial and enforcement authorities to the rights of the poor, women, children and 
minorities. 
The strategy will be to support law formulation and amendment with a view to closing the gap between 
international and national legislation, to support the development of affirmative action policies, and assisting 
in building the capacity of civil and political institutions including the Judiciary. 
More specifically, the UNCT will: 
(i) Support the monitoring and implementation of human rights instruments. 
The UN will provide technical and other assistance to Government for the implementation and 
strengthening of programmes of action on the CEDAW and on the CRC. The UNCT will direct technical 
assistance at the GHRC with a view to building capacity, improving the investigation of cases, and 
undertaking advocacy and support for publicity of the Commission’s work. 
(ii) Support the development of affirmative action policies and programmes for women 
and minorities. 
The UNCT will support actions aimed at ensuring the effective participation of women in family, community, 
private, and public life. This support will deal with legal and administrative factors, as well as traditional 
customary factors at the community level that permit discrimination and marginalization. The UNCT will 
support the establishment and proper functioning of an Ethnic Relations Commission and a Women’s 
Commission. 
(iii) Support institutional strengthening and capacity building of political institutions 
(parliament and local government) and civil society (CBOs, media). 
The CCA has been updated to reflect some of the more recent development in Guyana. Consistent with 
this update, the UNDAF will address assistance in the areas of coordination of assistance for the 
monitoring of general elections due to be held in January 2001. In addition, the UNCT will continue its 
financial and technical support for the Constitutional reform process. The UNCT will continue to support 
the integration of Constitutional reform proposals into draft legislation for parliamentary approval. 20
(iv) Support capacity-building of the Judiciary and enforcement authorities to ensure 
the rule of law and protections of human rights. 
In this regard, the UNCT will support Government in its continued efforts, in combination with bilateral 
donor assistance, to upgrade and modernize the judicial system and law enforcement. Attention will be 
given to the special support needed for cases of domestic violence. 
iv Follow-up and Review Mechanisms 
A. Follow-up 
In order to ensure the progressive realization of these rights, the UNCT will focus on the most vulnerable 
groups as a matter of priority and continue to promote participation, social mobilization, and 
decentralisation in the interest of enhancing participation and a more efficient use of available resources. 
The mainstreaming of gender issues, nutrition, reproductive health, and HIV/AIDS will all be accorded a 
high priority and will be pursued wherever possible at both the policy and community levels. 
Based on the UNDAF, all UN agencies, funds and programme will develop a complementary set of 
individual projects and programmes that will create numerous opportunities for joint programmes. The 
preparatory process of the CCA/UNDAF was invaluable in terms of development of stronger partnerships, 
increased networking among development organizations, greater exchange of information and expertise, 
and more focused and collaborative UN System participation in development co-operation. The UNCT will 
build on this process to consolidate its position as a partner in development and will continue its support to 
inter- and intra-sectoral coordination. The UN Country Team will also follow-up on these partnerships to 
secure additional resources in support of national needs and priorities. 
In keeping with its results oriented programming approach, the UNCT intends to set up a joint GovernmentUN Task-Force to look at ways of simplifying and harmonizing the programming and operational 
procedures in Guyana including formats of the project document, monitoring, reporting and evaluation 
mechanisms. 
B. Monitoring and evaluation 
Joint and parallel UNCT programmes will be monitored jointly, using common monitoring and reporting 
mechanisms. This will also contribute to reduce the burden for the government. Progress towards the 
goals and objectives of assistance will be assessed every year through a UNDAF Task Force composed of 
representatives from Government and the UN agencies. Thematic Groups will be responsible for 
monitoring results and updating indicators. This yearly assessment will be presented in the Annual Report 
of the UN Resident Coordinator (RC). The Midterm Reviews of the Country Programmes of individual 
agencies will also analyze progress towards the objectives of the UNDAF. This information too will be fed 
into the Annual Report of the RC. 
A Mid-Term Review of the UNDAF will be undertaken around June 2002. This review will examine the 
extent to which the UNDAF has met its basic purpose, assess the achievement of selected objectives, and 
taking stock of the lessons learnt with a view to strengthening the next UNDAF. The Mid-Term Review will 
be led jointly by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the UNRC. 21
VI ANNEXES
SELECTED ARTICLES FROM CONVENTIONS TO WHICH GUYANA IS A SIGNATORY
Convention on the Rights of the Child
Article 19
1. States Parties shall take all appropriate legislative, administrative, social and educational measures to 
protect the child from all forms of physical or mental violence, injury or abuse, neglect or negligent 
treatment, maltreatment or exploitation, including sexual abuse, while in the care of parent(s), legal 
guardian(s) or any other person who has the care of the child. 
2. Such protective measures should, as appropriate, include effective procedures for the establishment of 
social programmes to provide necessary support for the child and for those who have the care of the child, 
as well as for other forms of prevention and for identification, reporting, referral, investigation, treatment and 
follow-up of instances of child maltreatment described heretofore, and, as appropriate, for judicial 
involvement. 
Article 24 
1. States Parties recognise the right of the child to the enjoyment of the highest attainable standard of 
health and to facilities for the treatment of illness and rehabilitation of health. States Parties shall strive to 
ensure that no child is deprived of his or her right of access to such health care services. 
2. States Parties shall pursue full implementation of this right and, in particular, shall take appropriate 
measures: 
(a) To diminish infant and child mortality; 
(b) To ensure the provision of necessary medical assistance and health care to all children with emphasis 
on the development of primary health care; 
(c) To combat disease and malnutrition, including within the framework of primary health care, through, 
inter alia, the application of readily available technology and through the provision of adequate nutritious 
foods and clean drinking-water, taking into consideration the dangers and risks of environmental pollution; 
(d) To ensure appropriate pre-natal and post-natal health care for mothers; 
(e) To ensure that all segments of society, in particular parents and children, are informed, have access to 
education and are supported in the use of basic knowledge of child health and nutrition, the advantages of 
breastfeeding, hygiene and environmental sanitation and the prevention of accidents; 
(f) To develop preventive health care, guidance for parents and family planning education and services. 
3. States Parties shall take all effective and appropriate measures with a view to abolishing traditional 
practices prejudicial to the health of children. 
4. States Parties undertake to promote and encourage international co-operation with a view to achieving 
progressively the full realisation of the right recognised in the present article. In this regard, particular 
account shall be taken of the needs of developing countries. 22
Article 28 
1. States Parties recognise the right of the child to education, and with a view to achieving this right 
progressively and on the basis of equal opportunity, they shall, in particular: 
(a) Make primary education compulsory and available free to all; 
(b) Encourage the development of different forms of secondary education, including general and vocational 
education, make them available and accessible to every child, and take appropriate measures such as the 
introduction of free education and offering financial assistance in case of need; 
(c) Make higher education accessible to all on the basis of capacity by every appropriate means; 
(d) Make educational and vocational information and guidance available and accessible to all children; 
(e) Take measures to encourage regular attendance at schools and the reduction of drop-out rates. 
2. States Parties shall take all appropriate measures to ensure that school discipline is administered in a 
manner consistent with the child's human dignity and in conformity with the present Convention. 
3. States Parties shall promote and encourage international cooperation in matters relating to education, in 
particular with a view to contributing to the elimination of ignorance and illiteracy throughout the world and 
facilitating access to scientific and technical knowledge and modern teaching methods. In this regard, 
particular account shall be taken of the needs of developing countries. 
Article 32
1. States Parties recognise the right of the child to be protected from economic exploitation and from 
performing any work that is likely to be hazardous or to interfere with the child's education, or to be harmful 
to the child's health or physical, mental, spiritual, moral or social development. 
2. States Parties shall take legislative, administrative, social and educational measures to ensure the 
implementation of the present article. To this end, and having regard to the relevant provisions of other 
international instruments, States Parties shall in particular: (a) Provide for a minimum age or minimum ages 
for admission to employment; 
(b) Provide for appropriate regulation of the hours and conditions of employment; 
(c) Provide for appropriate penalties or other sanctions to ensure the effective enforcement of the present 
article. 
Article 33 
States Parties shall take all appropriate measures, including legislative, administrative, social and 
educational measures, to protect children from the illicit use of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances 
as defined in the relevant international treaties, and to prevent the use of children in the illicit production 
and trafficking of such substances. 
Article 34
States Parties undertake to protect the child from all forms of sexual exploitation and sexual abuse. For 
these purposes, States Parties shall in particular take all appropriate national, bilateral and multilateral 
measures to prevent: 
(a) The inducement or coercion of a child to engage in any unlawful sexual activity; 23
(b) The exploitative use of children in prostitution or other unlawful sexual practices; 
(c) The exploitative use of children in pornographic performances and materials. 
Article 37
States Parties shall ensure that: 
(a) No child shall be subjected to torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment. 
Neither capital punishment nor life imprisonment without possibility of release shall be imposed for offences 
committed by persons below eighteen years of age; 
 (b) No child shall be deprived of his or her liberty unlawfully or arbitrarily. The arrest, detention or 
imprisonment of a child shall be in conformity with the law and shall be used only as a measure of last 
resort and for the shortest appropriate period of time; 
(c) Every child deprived of liberty shall be treated with humanity and respect for the inherent dignity of the 
human person, and in a manner which takes into account the needs of persons of his or her age. In 
particular, every child deprived of liberty shall be separated from adults unless it is considered in the child's 
best interest not to do so and shall have the right to maintain contact with his or her family through 
correspondence and visits, save in exceptional circumstances; 
(d) Every child deprived of his or her liberty shall have the right to prompt access to legal and other 
appropriate assistance, as well as the right to challenge the legality of the deprivation of his or her liberty 
before a court or other competent, independent and impartial authority, and to a prompt decision on any 
such action. 
International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights
Article 2
1. Each State Party to the present Covenant undertakes to respect and to ensure to all individuals within 
its territory and subject to its jurisdiction the rights recognised in the present Covenant, without distinction 
of any kind, such as race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social 
origin, property, birth or other status. 
2. Where not already provided for by existing legislative or other measures, each State Party to the 
present Covenant undertakes to take the necessary steps, in accordance with its constitutional processes 
and with the provisions of the present Covenant, to adopt such laws or other measures as may be 
necessary to give effect to the rights recognised in the present Covenant. 
Article 3 
The States Parties to the present Covenant undertake to ensure the equal right of men and women to the 
enjoyment of all civil and political rights set forth in the present Covenant.
Article 6 
1. Every human being has the inherent right to life. This right shall be protected by law. No one shall be 
arbitrarily deprived of his life. 
2. In countries which have not abolished the death penalty, sentence of death may be imposed only for 
the most serious crimes in accordance with the law in force at the time of the commission of the crime 
and not contrary to the provisions of the present Covenant and to the Convention on the Prevention and 24
Punishment of the Crime of Genocide. This penalty can only be carried out pursuant to a final judgement 
rendered by a competent court. 
4. Anyone sentenced to death shall have the right to seek pardon or commutation of the sentence. 
Amnesty, pardon or commutation of the sentence of death may be granted in all cases. 
5. Sentence of death shall not be imposed for crimes committed by persons below eighteen years of age 
and shall not be carried out on pregnant women. 
Article 7 
No one shall be subjected to torture or to cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment. In 
particular, no one shall be subjected without his free consent to medical or scientific experimentation. 
Article 9 
1. Everyone has the right to liberty and security of person. No one shall be subjected to arbitrary arrest or 
detention. No one shall be deprived of his liberty except on such grounds and in accordance with such 
procedure as are established by law. 
2. Anyone who is arrested shall be informed, at the time of arrest, of the reasons for his arrest and shall 
be promptly informed of any charges against him. 
3. Anyone arrested or detained on a criminal charge shall be brought promptly before a judge or other 
officer authorised by law to exercise judicial power and shall be entitled to trial within a reasonable time or 
to release. It shall not be the general rule that persons awaiting trial shall be detained in custody, but 
release may be subject to guarantees to appear for trial, at any other stage of the judicial proceedings, 
and, should occasion arise, for execution of the judgement. 
4. Anyone who is deprived of his liberty by arrest or detention shall be entitled to take proceedings before 
a court, in order that court may decide without delay on the lawfulness of his detention and order his 
release if the detention is not lawful. 
5. Anyone who has been the victim of unlawful arrest or detention shall have an enforceable right to 
compensation. 
Article 17 
1. No one shall be subjected to arbitrary or unlawful interference with his privacy, family, home or 
correspondence, nor to unlawful attacks on his honour and reputation. 
2. Everyone has the right to the protection of the law against such interference or attacks. 
Article 18 
1. Everyone shall have the right to freedom of thought, conscience and religion. This right shall include 
freedom to have or to adopt a religion or belief of his choice, and freedom, either individually or in 
community with others and in public or private, to manifest his religion or belief in worship, observance, 
practice and teaching. 
2. No one shall be subject to coercion which would impair his freedom to have or to adopt a religion or 
belief of his choice. 
3. Freedom to manifest one's religion or beliefs may be subject only to such limitations as are prescribed 
by law and are necessary to protect public safety, order, health, or morals or the fundamental rights and 
freedoms of others. 4. The States Parties to the present Covenant undertake to have respect for the 
liberty of parents and, when applicable, legal guardians to ensure the religious and moral education of 
their children in conformity with their own convictions. 
Article 19 
1. Everyone shall have the right to hold opinions without interference. 25
2. Everyone shall have the right to freedom of expression; this right shall include freedom to seek, receive 
and impart information and ideas of all kinds, regardless of frontiers, either orally, in writing or in print, in 
the form of art, or through any other media of his choice. 
Article 26 
All persons are equal before the law and are entitled without any discrimination to the equal protection of 
the law. In this respect, the law shall prohibit any discrimination and guarantee to all persons equal and 
effective protection against discrimination on any ground such as race, colour, sex, language, religion, 
political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status. 
Article 27 
In those States in which ethnic, religious or linguistic minorities exist, persons belonging to such minorities 
shall not be denied the right, in community with the other members of their group, to enjoy their own 
culture, to profess and practise their own religion, or to use their own language. 
Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination 
against Women 
C. Article 2 
States Parties condemn discrimination against women in all its forms, agree to pursue by all appropriate 
means and without delay a policy of eliminating discrimination against women and, to this end, undertake: 
(a) To embody the principle of the equality of men and women in their national constitutions or other 
appropriate legislation if not yet incorporated therein and to ensure, through law and other appropriate 
means, the practical realisation of this principle; 
(b) To adopt appropriate legislative and other measures, including sanctions where appropriate, 
prohibiting all discrimination against women; 
(c) To establish legal protection of the rights of women on an equal basis with men and to ensure through 
competent national tribunals and other public institutions the effective protection of women against any 
act of discrimination; 
(d) To refrain from engaging in any act or practice of discrimination against women and to ensure that 
public authorities and institutions shall act in conformity with this obligation; 
(e) To take all appropriate measures to eliminate discrimination against women by any person, 
organisation or enterprise; 
 (f) To take all appropriate measures, including legislation, to modify or abolish existing laws, regulations, 
customs and practices which constitute discrimination against women; 
(g) To repeal all national penal provisions which constitute discrimination against women. 
Article 7 
States Parties shall take all appropriate measures to eliminate discrimination against women in the 
political and public life of the country and, in particular, shall ensure to women, on equal terms with men, 
the right: 
(a) To vote in all elections and public referenda and to be eligible for election to all publicly elected 
bodies; 
 (b) To participate in the formulation of government policy and the implementation thereof and to hold 
public office and perform all public functions at all levels of government; 26
 (c) To participate in non-governmental organisations and associations concerned with the public and 
political life of the country. 
Article 11 
1. States Parties shall take all appropriate measures to eliminate discrimination against women in the 
field of employment in order to ensure, on a basis of equality of men and women, the same rights, in 
particular: 
(a) The right to work as an inalienable right of all human beings; 
 (b) The right to the same employment opportunities, including the application of the same criteria for 
selection in matters of employment; 
 (c) The right to free choice of profession and employment, the right to promotion, job security and all 
benefits and conditions of service and the right to receive vocational training and retraining, including 
apprenticeships, advanced vocational training and recurrent training; 
 (d) The right to equal remuneration, including benefits, and to equal treatment in respect of work of equal 
value, as well as equality of treatment in the evaluation of the quality of work; 
2. In order to prevent discrimination against women on the grounds of marriage or maternity and to 
ensure their effective right to work, States Parties shall take appropriate measures: 
(a) To prohibit, subject to the imposition of sanctions, dismissal on the grounds of pregnancy or of 
maternity leave and discrimination in dismissals on the basis of marital status; 
(b) To introduce maternity leave with pay or with comparable social benefits without loss of former 
employment, seniority or social allowances; 
International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination 
Article 2 
1. States Parties condemn racial discrimination and undertake to pursue by all appropriate means 
and without delay a policy of eliminating racial discrimination in all its forms and promoting 
understanding among all races, and, to this end: 
(a) Each State Party undertakes to engage in no act or
practice of racial discrimination against persons,
groups of persons or institutions and to en sure that
all public authorities and public institutions, national
and local, shall act in conformity with this obligation;
(b) Each State Party undertakes not to sponsor, defend
or support racial discrimination by any persons or
organizations;
(c) Each State Party shall take effective measures to
review governmental, national and local policies, and to27
amend, rescind or nullify any laws and regulations which
have the effect of creating or perpetuating racial
discrimination wherever it exists;
(d) Each State Party shall prohibit and bring to an end,
by all appropriate means, including legislation as
required by circumstances, racial discrimination by any
persons, group or organization;
(e) Each State Party undertakes to encourage, where
appropriate, integrationist multiracial organizations
and movements and other means of eliminating barriers
between races, and to discourage anything which tends to
strengthen racial division.
2. States Parties shall, when the circumstances so warrant, take,
in the social, economic, cultural and other fields, special and
concrete measures to ensure the adequate development and
protection of certain racial groups or individuals belonging to
them, for the purpose of guaranteeing them the full and equal
enjoyment of human rights and fundamental freedoms. These measures
shall in no case en tail as a con sequence the maintenance of
unequal or separate rights for different racial groups after the
objectives for which they were taken have been achieved.
Article 4
States Parties condemn all propaganda and all organizations which
are based on ideas or theories of superiority of one race or group
of persons of one colour or ethnic origin, or which attempt to
justify or promote racial hatred and discrimination in any form,
and undertake to adopt immediate and positive measures designed to
eradicate all incitement to, or acts of, such discrimination and,
to this end, with due regard to the principles embodied in the
Universal Declaration of Human Rights and the rights expressly set
forth in article 5 of this Convention, inter alia:
(a) Shall declare an offence punishable by law all
dissemination of ideas based on racial superiority or
hatred, incitement to racial discrimination, as well as
all acts of violence or incitement to such acts against
any race or group of persons of another colour or ethnic
origin, and also the provision of any assistance to
racist activities, including the financing thereof;
(b) Shall declare illegal and prohibit organizations,
and also organized and all other propaganda activities,
which promote and incite racial discrimination, and
shall recognize participation in such organizations or
activities as an offence punishable by law;
(c) Shall not permit public authorities or public
institutions, national or local, to promote or incite
racial discrimination.
